source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 15); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 14 pages, 1 information sheet and an answer book of 28 pages, which is not in this PDF. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.stem_md:
The table below shows the time (in seconds, rounded to ONE decimal place) taken by $12$ athletes to run the $100$ metre sprint and the distance (in metres, rounded to ONE decimal place) of their best long jump.

The scatter plot representing the data above is given below.

The equation of the least squares regression line is $\hat{y}=a+bx$.

table.caption: 100 m sprint times and best long-jump distances of 12 athletes
rows: Distance of best long jump (in metres)

questions.text_md: An athlete runs the $100$ metre sprint in $11,7$ seconds. Use $\hat{y}=a+bx$ to predict the distance of the best long jump of this athlete.

Another athlete completes the $100$ metre sprint in $12,3$ seconds and the distance of his best long jump is $7,6$ metres. If this is included in the data, will the gradient of the least squares regression line increase or decrease? Motivate your answer without any further calculations.

questions.stem_md: In an experiment, a group of $23$ girls were presented with a page containing $30$ coloured rectangles. They were asked to name the colours of the rectangles correctly as quickly as possible. The time, in seconds, taken by each of the girls is given in the table below.

table.caption: Times (in seconds) taken by 23 girls to name the colours correctly

questions.stem_md: Calculate:

questions.text_md: The interquartile range of the data
The standard deviation of the times taken by the girls is $5,94$. How many girls took longer than ONE standard deviation from the mean to name the colours?
Draw a box and whisker diagram to represent the data on the number line provided in the ANSWER BOOK.

questions.stem_md: The five-number summary of the times taken by a group of $23$ boys in naming the colours of the rectangles correctly is $(15\,;\,21\,;\,23,5\,;\,26\,;\,38)$.

questions.text_md: Which of the two groups, girls or boys, had the lower median time to correctly name the colours of the rectangles?
The first three learners who named the colours of all $30$ rectangles correctly in the shortest time will receive a prize. How many boys will be among these three prizewinners? Motivate your answer.

The coordinates of $\mathrm{G}$ if the equation of $\mathrm{BG}$ is $7x-10y=8$
Show by calculation that the coordinates of $\mathrm{A}$ is $(2\,;\,5)$.
$\mathrm{ABCD}$ is a parallelogram with $\mathrm{D}$ in the first quadrant. Calculate the coordinates of $\mathrm{D}$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\mathrm{P}(-4\,;\,5)$ and $\mathrm{K}(0\,;\,-3)$ are the end points of the diameter of a circle with centre $\mathrm{M}$. $\mathrm{S}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are respectively the $x$- and $y$-intercept of the tangent to the circle at $\mathrm{P}$. $\theta$ is the inclination of $\mathrm{PK}$ with the positive $x$-axis.

The equation of the circle in the form $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}=r^{2}$
The equation of the tangent to the circle at $\mathrm{K}$ in the form $y=mx+c$
Determine the values of $t$ such that the line $y=\dfrac{1}{2}x+t$ cuts the circle at two different points.

**Without using a calculator**, determine the value of:
Prove:
In the diagram, the graph of $f(x)=\cos 2x$ is drawn for the interval $x\in[-270^{\circ}\,;\,90^{\circ}]$.

questions.text_md: Draw the graph of $g(x)=2\sin x-1$ for the interval $x\in[-270^{\circ}\,;\,90^{\circ}]$ on the grid given in your ANSWER BOOK. Show ALL the intercepts with the axes, as well as the turning points.
Let $\mathrm{A}$ be a point of intersection of the graphs of $f$ and $g$. Show that the $x$-coordinate of $\mathrm{A}$ satisfies the equation $\sin x=\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$.
Hence, calculate the coordinates of the points of intersection of graphs of $f$ and $g$ for the interval $x\in[-270^{\circ}\,;\,90^{\circ}]$.

questions.stem_md: $\mathrm{AB}$ represents a vertical netball pole. Two players are positioned on either side of the netball pole at points $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{E}$ such that $\mathrm{D}$, $\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{E}$ are on the same straight line. A third player is positioned at $\mathrm{C}$. The points $\mathrm{B}$, $\mathrm{C}$, $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{E}$ are in the same horizontal plane. The angles of elevation from $\mathrm{C}$ to $\mathrm{A}$ and from $\mathrm{E}$ to $\mathrm{A}$ are $x$ and $y$ respectively. The distance from $\mathrm{B}$ to $\mathrm{E}$ is $k$.

questions.text_md: If it is further given that $\mathrm{D}\hat{\mathrm{A}}\mathrm{C}=2x$ and $\mathrm{AD}=\mathrm{AC}$, show that the distance $\mathrm{DC}$ between the players at $\mathrm{D}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ is $2k\tan y$.
